tone_patterns: Formal, institutional voice using third-person references to the reporting entity (e.g., “the Group”).
Balanced framing that acknowledges limitations and uncertainty while signalling intent and direction.
Forward-looking language used cautiously (e.g., indicating planned enhancements and future disclosures).
Risk-and-opportunity duality maintained throughout, often pairing constraints with strategic responses.
Use of measured confidence statements without absolute certainty; avoids overly promotional phrasing.
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a problem-definition paragraph describing analytical/data challenges before introducing actions.
Uses short, logically sequenced paragraphs that move from context → challenge → response → outlook.
Includes explicit caveats about maturity/early-stage programmes before stating current-period implications.
Employs bridging sentences that reference other report sections for detail, avoiding repetition.
Introduces lists after a lead-in sentence (e.g., “strategy focuses on” / “we seek to”), then returns to narrative.
heading_patterns: Numbered sub-sections within Strategy (e.g., multi-level numbering such as 3.x) to map to disclosure requirements.
Headings are descriptive and disclosure-oriented (e.g., impacts on strategy/decision-making; financial effects).
Standalone topic labels (e.g., “Physical Risks”, “Opportunities”) appear as navigational markers preceding narrative.
Consistent repetition of the section title in page headers/footers to reinforce location within the report.
pdf_layout_patterns: Multi-page section with consistent footer containing section name, page number, and report title line.
Page begins with continuation narrative, then transitions into a numbered subheading block.
Bulleted lists are formatted with clear indentation and line wrapping aligned to bullet text.
Use of whitespace between paragraphs and before lists to visually separate concepts.
Occasional mid-page navigational labels (topic markers) used to segment content without a full page break.
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses disclosure-style qualifiers such as “at this stage” and “in the current reporting period” to scope statements.
Explicitly states when there are no items to report (e.g., no trade-offs; no reportable financial implications yet).
References alignment with external frameworks/standard-setter developments in a non-committal monitoring posture.
Connects strategy statements to governance and risk management structures using cross-references.
Defines or introduces named frameworks/instruments with parenthetical shorthand, then uses the shorthand thereafter.
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented as process-based (actions underway, programmes being established) rather than outcome-heavy.
Uses selective quantitative evidence as illustrative scale markers, embedded within narrative paragraphs.
Supports credibility by citing external validation/assurance-type artifacts (e.g., independent opinions) in principle.
Anchors statements to time (e.g., reporting period, as-at date) when presenting status or financing activity.
Uses comparative/relative framing (e.g., “largest”, “milestone”) as emphasis, typically tied to a specific event.
section_specific_observations: Strategy content is structured to cover: data/assessment capability constraints, strategic commitments, integration into decision-making, and financial effects.
Physical risk discussion emphasizes data granularity (spatial and temporal) as a prerequisite for assessment quality.
Transition from qualitative strategy to governance linkage occurs in later sub-sections, reinforcing connectivity across pillars.
Trade-offs are treated as a discrete disclosure item with an explicit statement even when none are identified.
Financial effects subsection distinguishes between current-period reportable impacts and ongoing assessment work.
things_to_avoid_copying: Any entity-specific commitments, financing volumes, dates, or claims of market leadership.
Any references to specific countries, national plans, or jurisdictional targets as if universally applicable.
Names of external organisations providing opinions/assessments, and any branded framework titles.
Any statements implying alignment with a particular national pathway or policy instrument.
Any specific governance body names/titles or organisational structures beyond generic descriptions.
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Entity name and report title identifiers.
Specific monetary amounts, issuance sizes, and financing totals.
Specific years, as-at dates, and time-bound targets.
References to a particular jurisdiction’s national commitments and neutrality timeline.
Mentions of specific third-party providers of independent opinions.
Claims of being the largest issuer in a named region and related superlatives.
References to specific governance bodies and committees by name.
